races.name: Trustmark Apprentice Handicap

runners_data.name: Level Up
runners_data.note: A 7-year-old hold-up type with solid course-distance form on Good, consistent place strikes but no win from 15 similar-going runs; Alexandra McDonnell's 7lb claim is the main positive, but this horse needs the pace to lift late and is vulnerable in a muddled-gallop sprint.|

runners_data.name: Sonic Si
runners_data.note: Back-to-back winner including on Good ground, the most in-form runner here; Matthew Lloyd Slater's 5lb claim adds appeal, and on the best recent evidence this horse has the class and momentum to travel handy and strike in a compressed finish.|

runners_data.name: Vape
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up type with a natural preference for sitting deep, displaced to a midfield mapping because of the congested rear; despite two wins on Good ground, its recent form string includes several poor efforts, and at 9 years old with a 19-day break it faces questions about recapturing that level — style fit is reduced here.|

runners_data.name: So Smart
runners_data.note: Headgear (tp) suggests a horse that has needed restraining, and Grace Harris's runners have modest 14-day figures; a true hold-up operator pushed into a midfield role in this race shape, and its recent form shows no win in five turf runs on similar going, making it hard to enthuse about.|

runners_data.name: Hallandale Beach
runners_data.note: The only unknown-style runner in the field, a 3-year-old with no confirmed front-running or hold-up profile; has placed twice on Good ground including at this distance, the light weight of 135lbs helps, and Kevin Philippart De Foy's runner could be dangerous if Taryn Langley secures an early position that the other hold-up types cannot.|

runners_data.name: Bridget's Baby
runners_data.note: A lightly-raced 3-year-old with a best effort of second over 5f on Good — the most relevant form — but more typically a hold-up horse whose four recent runs include one win in that style; Myla Coppins's 5lb claim is the attraction, though the low OR of 50 and the fact this horse tends to get shuffled back means it is relying on others to set things up.|

races.paceDynamic: With no confirmed front-runner in this six-runner 5f handicap at Ffos Las, the race is likely to drift into a compressed, sprint-finish contest where position in the early stages is largely self-selecting. Hallandale Beach is the one unknown-style runner who could push forward, while the field is otherwise populated by hold-up types who will be jockeying for cover rather than daylight. On Good turf over five furlongs, that scenario typically produces a wall-to-wall gallop from those who do establish early, rewarding horses who can quicken late from a handy enough spot rather than deep closers who need a true scorching pace to pull clear. The field holds more hold-up types than the track can genuinely accommodate at the rear — Vape, So Smart, and Bridget's Baby are all true hold-up horses but have been mapped to midfield given the congestion, meaning none of them is guaranteed their natural racing position; of the three, Vape's experience at 9 and prior course-suitable form gives it the best chance of getting organised. The race shape favours a horse who settles just off whatever modest early pace emerges and times a run from mid-pack — a prominent-to-midfield cruiser with a strong finishing kick on Good ground is ideally placed.

Vape, So Smart, and Bridget's Baby all competing for space at the rear could produce racing interference in the early stages; watch for any of the three being checked or switched wide entering the final two furlongs.|

Sonic Si's back-to-back form gives it clear momentum, but if Matthew Lloyd Slater elects to drop in rather than push forward, the pace advantage is wasted and the horse becomes just another horse chasing a modest gallop.|

Good ground confirmed throughout the card at Ffos Las; no going concern applies to any runner here, but Level Up's best similar-going strike rate (3 places from 15) is notably modest and should temper enthusiasm despite the surface suitability.|

races.name: Carmarthenshire Hunt Restricted Maiden Fillies' Stakes (Bands C and D) (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Cavan Lady
runners_data.note: Lightly raced two-year-old for Richard Hughes with Finley Marsh up, third on debut at five furlongs on soft — the step up to good ground is a legitimate question mark, but the five-furlong trip repeats and her unknown ceiling leaves her relevant in a weak maiden; style unclassified so positional neutrality is an asset here.

runners_data.name: Nasserein
runners_data.note: Archie Watson's filly — a yard with a solid two-year-old record — fifth at six furlongs on firm on debut and now drops in trip to five furlongs on good ground, which is a key unknown; Pierre-Louis Jamin takes the ride and the shortening of the distance may suit if she has speed to burn, though the form line is thin.

runners_data.name: Tango Hotel
runners_data.note: George Scott runner who has shown finishing form behind the leaders (fourth and fifth at five furlongs) and whose best piece of form comes at this distance on good ground — the sim-going flag of one placed run in two outings on similar conditions is the most relevant angle here; Liam Wright's claim saves weight and the hood suggests minor headgear experimentation.

runners_data.name: Defiant Dream
runners_data.note: Mark Usher's filly holds her best chance if pace truly materialises, but a ninth on debut at six furlongs on standard and a fading profile mean optimism must be limited; her true running style is hold-up but the race map has her in midfield because there are more rear-of-field types than the shape can honestly place at the back — racing further forward than natural won't resolve her finish-line tendency to fade.

runners_data.name: Leading Raya
runners_data.note: Also trained by Mark Usher and also carrying a fade flag, she finished tenth at six furlongs on soft and is now taking on a shorter trip on better ground — neither the form nor the profile suggests she can convert to a more prominent role, and an apprentice booking (Rose Dawes, 5lb) won't mask a fundamental tactical problem in a small field at five furlongs.

runners_data.name: Past Passion
runners_data.note: Jonathan Portman's filly has run twice at five furlongs on good, placing second first time out before a seventh, and is the race's only confirmed front-runner — the 40-day layoff is worth monitoring but on good ground at this trip she is likely to dictate; her STYLE_FIT flag acknowledges she may not be in her very sharpest role, but in this field no other horse will take the lead from her.

races.paceDynamic: Past Passion is the sole confirmed front-runner in a six-runner field and is expected to bowl along at a sustainable, uncontested pace over five furlongs on good ground at Ffos Las — a flat, galloping track that rewards horses who travel economically in front. With no genuine rival to challenge Past Passion for the lead, the pace is unlikely to be truly strong, which shortens the race into a test of who can sustain momentum into the final furlong rather than who can finish from off the bridle. The hold-up horses — Defiant Dream and Leading Raya — both carry fade flags and face a compounded problem: with two lightly raced unknowns (Cavan Lady and Nasserein) and Tango Hotel likely to press or sit close to the pace, there is no truly deep field to work through and little likelihood of a strong enough gallop to bring the closers into play. This race shape strongly favours horses able to race prominently or travel just off the pace, converting a controlled lead into a winning performance in the straight — true hold-up tactics on this flat five-furlong course in a small field are a structural disadvantage today. The field holds more hold-up types than the race shape can accommodate at the rear: Defiant Dream is mapped to midfield rather than the back, but neither it nor Leading Raya is well-served by the likely tempo.

watchPoints.text: Past Passion's 40-day break is the key risk factor — watch closely in the paddock and at the start for any sign of rustiness, as an uncontested lead from a flat track is hers to lose if she jumps cleanly.

Cavan Lady is lightly raced with an unclassified style — if Finley Marsh sends her forward aggressively, she could complicate Past Passion's lead plans and force a higher early tempo than the race map anticipates.

Both Mark Usher runners (Defiant Dream and Leading Raya) carry fade flags — if either tries to race closer to the pace than their natural style dictates, they risk burning out before the furlong pole and leaving a false impression of early competitiveness.

Tango Hotel's hood is worth noting — George Scott horses in headgear at this level sometimes show marked improvement, and her sim-going placed run makes her the main beneficiary if the pace is genuinely competitive rather than processional.

races.name: Blackmore Building Contractors Handicap

runners_data.name: Senor Campanaro
runners_data.note: A hold-up performer for Ed Walker whose best form on similar going shows limited return (0 wins, 0 places from 3 sim-going runs), though his one win came over 7f at Standard — the trip is fine but the soft-ground form profile and 26 days off invite caution; Ashley Lewis claims 5lb.

runners_data.name: Katie's Song
runners_data.note: Richard Hughes has a solid 14-day strike rate (5/24) and Finley Marsh takes the ride on this hold-up filly whose limited form string (5-0-6) over this sort of trip on Standard ground leaves plenty of questions unanswered at Ffos Las.

runners_data.name: Who Is Alice
runners_data.note: Grace Harris's filly has a history of running over 6f and steps up to 7½f here, which looks a potential concern given all five career runs have been at shorter trips; her sim-going record (1 win, 2 places from 10 runs) is the most encouraging going angle in the field, but the extra furlong is untested.

runners_data.name: Kingofthecarnival
runners_data.note: Archie Watson's colt wore a hood on his last run and has a win over 7f on Standard — form-wise the most interesting runner in the field — but his natural hold-up style means he is operating without his preferred rear-of-field berth in this pace-starved contest, which will compromise how effectively he can produce his finish.

runners_data.name: Red Moon
runners_data.note: Jack Channon's improving three-year-old ran just three days ago (1/7f/GOO), which demands close scrutiny, and while his sim-going record (1 win, 1 place from 4 runs on Good) is genuinely encouraging, the very quick turnaround and the reality that his hold-up style is likely to place him closer than natural in this field tempers enthusiasm.

runners_data.name: Thai Princess
runners_data.note: Andrew Balding's filly carries a hood (headgear noted) and returns after 51 days off — the longest break in the field — having posted three consecutive placed or mid-pack finishes at shorter trips; Callum Hutchinson takes the ride but the layoff, unproven trip, and redistribution away from her natural position all work against her.

runners_data.name: Gelato
runners_data.note: Adrian Wintle's 14-day record is a blank (0/9), and Gelato's form on Good ground is consistently poor (0 wins, 0 places from 7 sim-going runs), making this a difficult one to recommend regardless of positional considerations; her 5f and 6f form profile also raises the question of whether 7½f is simply too far.

runners_data.name: Phantom Shadow
runners_data.note: Harry Charlton's colt has his two best form figures over 8f on Fibresand (3rd and 2nd), and his placed record on sim-going (0 wins, 0 places from 6 runs) is moderate, though the step back slightly in trip from those runs may actually suit if this race turns into a stamina test rather than a pure sprint; George Wood rides.

runners_data.name: Distillation
runners_data.note: Mark Usher's filly ran 15 days ago and has a second over 7f on Standard as her most recent highlight — modest form overall, and while her hold-up style theoretically fits a strong late-closing scenario, the race shape here gives her little pace to chase, undermining the utility of that profile.

races.paceDynamic: With no confirmed front-runner in this nine-runner 7½f handicap at Ffos Las, the early gallop is likely to be modest at best, with the entire field comprised of hold-up and midfield types jostling for position rather than setting any meaningful tempo. The pace dynamic note flags that Kingofthecarnival, Thai Princess, Red Moon, and Gelato are genuine hold-up horses redistributed into the midfield on the map because the field is so back-heavy — none of them is likely to secure a prominent berth naturally, though one or two may press forward by necessity in a field with no willing leader. The absence of any true pace-setter means the race will almost certainly crawl early, compress into a tight bunch through the middle stages, and develop into a sprint finish from the two-furlong pole — a stamina-sapping test of finishing kick on good turf rather than a true end-to-end gallop. This race shape strongly favours horses with a proven sharp turn of foot in a steadily-run contest, and any runner that can travel fluently in the pack and produce a sustained late burst will hold the clearest positional advantage; genuine hold-up horses racing out of role in a race with no pace to hold up to are significantly disadvantaged. The field is so uniformly hold-up in style that the horse which pragmatically takes up the best tactical position in a compressed field — without expending unnecessary energy — will likely dictate the finish.

watchPoints.text: Red Moon ran just three days ago — monitor any market moves and watch the paddock closely for signs of freshness or fatigue before committing to this runner.

With no front-runner in the field, watch for a false-start scramble for position in the early stages — any runner that gets badly squeezed or shuffled back at the break on a track where Ffos Las's layout punishes early trouble could be compromised immediately.

Kingofthecarnival wore headgear on his last run and is being asked to race out of his natural rear position — if he is forced wide or checks momentum in a bunched field, his ability to produce his best finish will be significantly reduced.
Who Is Alice attempts 7½f for the first time having run exclusively at 6f — watch her early to see if she travels smoothly or fades once the pace test truly begins in the final quarter-mile.

Phantom Shadow's best efforts came over 8f, and if this race is steadily run the extra furlong would likely have suited him — watch whether the pace develops enough to play to his staying profile or whether it remains a pure sprint that negates his stamina advantage.

races.name: RHN Travel Handicap

runners_data.name: Marlborough Place
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with good-ground form and a win over 8f suggesting stamina is not in doubt at 7½f; Taryn Langley's 5lb claim is useful, and after a 112-day break the yard's 1/11 strike rate over 14 days is worth noting — may need the run but the style profile puts her right in the firing line here.

runners_data.name: Huscal
runners_data.note: Thomas Greatrex takes the ride for Charles Hills who is in excellent 14-day form (3/13); wears a tongue-tie, has course-positive experience at this trip in similar going, and his consistent prominent style means he should sit in a natural position throughout — his recent form (5, 2, 8, 12) is mixed but the two placed efforts came at this trip on similar surfaces.

runners_data.name: Great Dream
runners_data.note: Haggas runner freshened up after just 5 days, carrying headgear (p); his natural instinct is to race prominently but with too many front-biased horses in the field he is likely to find himself further back than ideal, and his sim-going record of 3/9 without a win or place suggests the conditions do not bring out his best.

runners_data.name: Factual
runners_data.note: The one confirmed front-runner in the field, Andrew Balding's three-year-old has a win at 7f on good ground and a second at the same trip on the same surface — the form justifies his lead role and the absence of any serious pace challenger means he should face no early pressure; the STYLE_FIT flag reminds that his OR advantage may be somewhat offset by the redistribution dynamic pressing other horses onto him.

runners_data.name: Sunny Smile
runners_data.note: Hugo Palmer's filly wears a tongue-tie and returns after just 12 days; her best form has come over 6f and she is stepping up in trip, which is a question mark — the hold-up style means she depends on a strong pace being set, which this race shape may not provide, and her sim-going record (4/6) shows one win and two places but all on good-ground sprints.

runners_data.name: Dagger Strike
runners_data.note: Archie Watson's hold-up gelding wears a hood and has a striking record of placing (2nd four times in his last five) without winning; the 39-day break is modest, and his consistent staying-on profile at 7f on good and standard-to-slow surfaces gives him place claims, but he needs the pace to be strong enough to close into — a slow-run race is his enemy.

runners_data.name: Slight Of Foot
runners_data.note: Harry Charlton's three-year-old wears a hood and has run at this trip repeatedly on Tapeta and good ground; a natural prominent type who is mapped to midfield because the field's pace cluster is too large to accommodate him up front, which materially reduces his chance — his sole good-ground sim-going placing was a second at 7f but his overall record in similar conditions (1/4) without a win reflects limited scope.

races.paceDynamic: Factual is the confirmed front-runner here and, with no rival willing or able to seriously dispute the lead at 7½f on good ground at Ffos Las, he should dictate at a comfortable, sustainable gallop rather than face any real pressure. Marlborough Place and Huscal are both prominent-style horses who will track Factual closely, creating a compact early order but not a contested pace that will burn the leader off. The field actually contains more prominent-profile horses than can physically occupy those front positions — Great Dream and Slight Of Foot are natural prominent runners who will be pushed into midfield against their instincts, which compromises their chance. This race shape — a controlled, unhurried pace set by a single front-runner — strongly favours horses with tactical speed who can race close to the action from the outset, making the prominent trackers (Marlborough Place, Huscal) best placed to pounce, while true hold-up horses Sunny Smile and Dagger Strike face a stern challenge if the pace is never strong enough to string the field out.

watchPoints.text: Factual — if he bowls clear unchallenged from the off, monitor whether any of Marlborough Place or Huscal press him before the straight, because a completely unchallenged lead on good ground at Ffos Las can be very hard to peg back in the final 1½f.

Great Dream and Slight Of Foot — both natural prominent horses squeezed into midfield by the pace cluster; watch their early positioning, because if either gets further back than a length or two off the leaders they are racing against their own instincts and their chance diminishes sharply.

Sunny Smile — stepping up from 6f to 7½f for the first time in this form cycle; if the pace is comfortable rather than strong, she will have nothing to close into and could be left flat-footed in the straight despite good-ground form.

Dagger Strike — four consecutive second-place finishes make him a notable each-way interest, but his hold-up profile means the pace dynamic is critical; if Factual dawdles, Dagger Strike's closing run will be blunted well before the line.

races.name: Blackmore Building Contractors Handicap

runners_data.name: Pay Attention
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up filly who has shown form over this distance on good ground (placed at 8f/GOO twice in recent hist), though her sim-going record of 1W5P from nine is modest; trainer Faye Bramley has just 1 win from 9 over 14 days and she may need things to fall perfectly from the rear.|

runners_data.name: Devious Devan
runners_data.note: Won last time out at 8f on standard going but carries a poor sim-going record on good (0W3P from 4 runs) and is a natural hold-up horse that will struggle to get to the rear here with so many others needing that ground; William Muir & Grassick yard is out of form at 0/11 in the last 14 days.|

runners_data.name: Rosemary's Rose
runners_data.note: Rod Millman's filly has shown she can place on good ground (2/7f/STA, 2/8f/STA) and has placed in 2 of her last 4 comparable outings; as a genuine closer now pushed into midfield by the field shape, she will need a strong pace to develop — which this race is unlikely to provide.|

runners_data.name: Bobby Dassler
runners_data.note: Won most recently at 8f on good ground in a career that spans longer trips (10-12f) and he carries headgear (t); his trainer Barry John Murphy has 2 from 11 in the last 14 days, and having raced just 2 days ago, freshness is a legitimate question — though he has a solid sim-going record of 1W3P from 7 comparable runs.|

runners_data.name: Fifty Sent
runners_data.note: The sole front-runner in the field, having won back-to-back at 8f on standard going, but his sim-going figures on good (0W0P from 2) are a minor concern; ridden by 7lb claimer Zoe Lewis, he will need to be allowed to roll along at his own tempo — if he does, the race is his to lose.|

runners_data.name: Quick Turn
runners_data.note: Three-year-old who landed an 8f win on standard and has a promising good-ground second (2/8f/GOO) in recent history; Harry Vigors (7lb claimer) takes off significant weight and his trainer Ian Williams, though quiet at 0/32 in 14 days, fields a horse with genuine tactical pace to track Fifty Sent closely.|

runners_data.name: Alice's Influence
runners_data.note: David Evans filly has won at 8f on good going and has placed in three of her last five, including a second at 8f/GOO, making her one of the more interesting good-ground performers in the race; as a true hold-up type now shifted toward midfield by field congestion, she benefits if she can secure cover and time her run — Evans is a sharp trainer at 4 from 14 in the last fortnight.|

runners_data.name: U S S Constitution
runners_data.note: Listed as a non-runner — disregard for race shape purposes; had he run, his hold-up style and strong sim-going record of 0W0P from 11 on good would have reinforced the crowded-closer problem in this field.|

races.paceDynamic: Fifty Sent is the lone confirmed front-runner in this eight-runner field and, with no genuine challenger to the lead expected, should be able to dictate a comfortable, sustainable gallop from the front over this flat Ffos Las mile on good ground. The pace is unlikely to be searingly strong, meaning the race will be run at a controlled tempo that keeps the field compressed and reduces the premium on closing speed from deep. This race shape strongly favours those who can track Fifty Sent at close range and pounce in the straight — prominent-to-midfield types who avoid cover and can deliver a sustained run rather than a late burst. The field contains a glut of genuine hold-up horses — Devious Devan, Rosemary's Rose, Bobby Dassler, Alice's Influence, and U S S Constitution are all redistributed to midfield on the map because the rear simply cannot accommodate this many true closers, meaning only those who adapt their position or get an unusually clean run will see their natural style rewarded.

watchPoints.text: Fifty Sent — monitor whether Zoe Lewis (7lb claimer) allows him to stride on uncontested from the gate; any hesitation establishing the lead early could compress the field and trigger a bunched finish that changes the entire race shape.

Quick Turn — at age 3 receiving weight from older rivals and ridden by a 7lb claimer, he gets a notable weight advantage; watch for him to be positioned no further than third entering the home straight, as that is where his profile works best in this pace scenario.

races.name: Oil 4 Wales Restricted Maiden Fillies' Stakes (Bands B, C And D) (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Poor Relation
runners_data.note: Ollie Sangster's filly arrives on an eight-day turnaround with a form string showing some consistency at shorter trips; she is the clear pace-setter here and her ability to control fractions is central to this race's shape, though a style fit flag tempers confidence she will produce a career-best once she commits to the lead role fully.

runners_data.name: Alikalu
runners_data.note: One of two Jack Jones debutantes — completely unknown quantity with no form or going data to work from; Pierre-Louis Jamin takes the ride and with an open style profile she could slot anywhere, making her a genuine wildcard whose price may not reflect her true chance.

runners_data.name: Blue Tulip
runners_data.note: Muir and Grassick's filly has shown modest form over 8-10f on Soft and Standard, and although her natural instinct is to race from the rear, the density of hold-up types in this field means she is unlikely to secure that position and will race closer to the pace than suits her best.

runners_data.name: Evening Fades
runners_data.note: William Haggas fields this filly with positive 1/2 similar-going placed form to her name; she wants to come from off the pace and the Good going is fine for her, though she will need the early gallop to be honest enough over 1m2f to bring her hold-up style into play late.

runners_data.name: Lady Magu
runners_data.note: Roger Varian's lightly raced filly has consecutive fifth-place finishes over 10f on Good and Standard — consistent without threatening — and Harry Vigors takes a claimer's allowance; her style is unconfirmed, which is a material unknown, and she has shown zero wins or places from two efforts at similar distances and going.

runners_data.name: Miss Malone To You
runners_data.note: Michael Bell's filly returns from a 53-day break wearing a hood, which is worth noting as a potential settling aid; she is a hold-up type with a form figure of fifth on Good ground over 10f, and the extended layoff combined with modest prior form makes her one to treat with caution despite the headgear sharpener.

runners_data.name: Ziata
runners_data.note: Ed Walker's filly carries a blinder and has solid placed form — a second from four runs with one placed effort on similar going — and her prominent racing style makes her a natural partner to Poor Relation at the head of affairs; she may be the most straightforward beneficiary if Poor Relation's gallop opens up enough of a gap early.

runners_data.name: Feelin' Free
runners_data.note: The second Jack Jones debutante on the card alongside Alikalu, ridden by Finley Marsh with no form or going history to assess; with an unknown style and no exposed form, she is a complete enigma though the trainer's two-from-eleven fourteen-day strike rate suggests the yard is not firing at maximum.

races.paceDynamic: Poor Relation is the one confirmed front runner in this eight-runner field and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, she should be able to slot into an uncontested position at the head of affairs and dictate a measured, sustainable gallop over Ffos Las's flat 1m2f circuit. Ziata also holds prominent tendencies and may push forward to track Poor Relation, but nothing in this field looks capable of forcing a genuinely searching pace that would compromise a well-positioned leader. Blue Tulip is a true hold-up type redistributed to midfield on the map because the field actually holds more prominent/hold-up runners than can all occupy their natural ground; Blue Tulip is unlikely to get her natural rear position and will race closer than ideal. With a single pace-setter dictating an honest-but-unchallenged tempo on a flat, galloping track, this race shape strongly favours horses who can race prominently or in a close-tracking position and sustain their effort through the final two furlongs — deep hold-up closers will find limited late room to reel in a front runner who has not been pressured.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Front-Runner Dictates
scenarios.trigger: If Poor Relation is allowed to stride into an uncontested lead and control fractions throughout.
scenarios.body: If Poor Relation is allowed to stride into an uncontested lead and control fractions throughout.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Tracker Swoops At Business End
scenarios.trigger: If Poor Relation's pace is slightly too slow and a prominent tracker produces the better finishing effort in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: If Poor Relation's pace is slightly too slow and a prominent tracker produces the better finishing effort in the final furlong.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Closer Lands Late
scenarios.trigger: If the genuine hold-up horses can find a clean passage and the early gallop proves honest enough to bring them into it.
scenarios.body: If the genuine hold-up horses can find a clean passage and the early gallop proves honest enough to bring them into it.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Field Bunches
scenarios.trigger: If Poor Relation fails to stride on and the field bunches into a sprint finish with no clear pace shape emerging.
scenarios.body: If Poor Relation fails to stride on and the field bunches into a sprint finish with no clear pace shape emerging.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Poor Relation is immediately pushed to the front from the gate or allows Ziata to test her for the lead — if a minor battle for the rail develops in the early stages, it could compress her energy reserves and change the entire race shape.

Blue Tulip will likely race closer than her natural style dictates due to the crowded hold-up contingent; if she ends up trapped in midfield traffic around the bend rather than finding a clean outside run, her chance is effectively gone.

Both Alikalu and Feelin' Free are Jack Jones debutantes with zero exposed form — if either is well-fancied in the market, treat that as an informed yard signal worth noting before concluding the race is Poor Relation's to control.

Evening Fades has the clearest similar-going placed form among the hold-up fillies; watch her position at the top of the straight — if she is within four lengths at the two-furlong pole she is the likeliest closer to pick off a tiring leader.

Miss Malone To You's hood is new headgear following a 53-day break — if she breaks smartly and settles in a prominent position rather than her usual hold-up role, the hood may be doing its job and she becomes more relevant to Scenario A or B than her style tag suggests.

races.name: Josh Perry BPRFC Supporters Player Of The Year Handicap

runners_data.name: Zooter
runners_data.note: Handles Good ground well (6/7 career runs on similar) and has placed at 10f before, making this trip credible; Finley Marsh rides for small yard Jack Jones (0 wins in 16 over 14 days) but Zooter's best form is a 2nd at 10f on Good and should settle naturally in a tactical race.

runners_data.name: Liveinthelight
runners_data.note: Ollie Sangster's yard is in decent 14-day form (6/22) but this horse has only won once in 11 career starts and fades in the finish; its true racing style is rear-division hold-up, displaced to a midfield mapping here because the entire field crowds the back of the field, so it faces a positional squeeze.

runners_data.name: Tales Old As Time
runners_data.note: Returns after a lengthy 237-day absence for a small yard with light recent activity, and the form figures of 380 include a heavy-ground Southwell run — Good ground here is unexplored territory for this two-year-old; a natural hold-up type who also fades in the stretch, making its reappearance credentials hard to assess confidently.

runners_data.name: Rajwaah
runners_data.note: Archie Watson (2/17 in 14 days) sends this three-year-old whose recent form reads 609 — placed once in three Good/Standard runs, but has faded in all three finishes; though mapped to midfield, its instinct is to race from the rear, and with the field already congested there, Pierre-Louis Jamin may struggle to find a clean passage late.

runners_data.name: Grand Pier
runners_data.note: Warren Greatrex saddles this six-run maiden who has shown up at 10f on Good before (6th, career best distance); Harry Vigors (7lb claimer) is a positive booking, but the horse has managed just three placed efforts in six career starts and, despite being a hold-up type by nature, is mapped forward because the rear is too crowded to accommodate everyone.

runners_data.name: Blue Jammin
runners_data.note: Most recent winner in the field (1st, 8f, Soft) and quickest to the track (9 days since last run) for Muir & Grassick; however, that win came on Soft and all four subsequent efforts on Good or Standard have produced no placing, raising a genuine going concern — Jack Dace's 5lb claim helps the weights but the step up in ground is a real risk.

races.paceDynamic: With all six runners carrying a hold-up profile and no confirmed front-runner in the field, this 1m2f contest at Ffos Las on Good ground faces a genuine leadership vacuum from the outset. The early stages are likely to be falsely run and dawdling, with horses reluctantly pushing forward before the tempo eventually picks up, compressing the race into a sprint finish over the final two furlongs. Zooter, Tales Old As Time, and Blue Jammin are among those who may find themselves drifting closer to the pace by default rather than by design, with none possessing the natural front-running profile to impose a true gallop. This shape theoretically favours whoever can produce the sharpest late turn of foot, but given the compressed, tactical nature of proceedings, the horse who can best handle a messy contest and produce a quick, decisive kick from a central position will hold the clearest edge — midfield-to-close types with a clean run will be most advantaged. Note that Liveinthelight, Rajwaah, Grand Pier, and Blue Jammin are all genuine hold-up horses redistributed into midfield on the map because the field holds more pure hold-up types than the race shape can accommodate at the rear simultaneously, meaning none are truly guaranteed to secure their preferred rearmost position.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Muddled Pace Sprint Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the early gallop is deliberately slow and the field concertinas into a bunched dash home over the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: If the early gallop is deliberately slow and the field concertinas into a bunched dash home over the final two furlongs.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Honest Gallop Suits Stayer
scenarios.trigger: If one runner edges forward to set a genuine, even pace that strings the field out over the full 1m2f trip.
scenarios.body: If one runner edges forward to set a genuine, even pace that strings the field out over the full 1m2f trip.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Positional Winner From Front
scenarios.trigger: If a runner edges unexpectedly wide and grabs a soft lead, controlling the race entirely unchallenged.
scenarios.body: If a runner edges unexpectedly wide and grabs a soft lead, controlling the race entirely unchallenged.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Late Closer Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If the race is set up with enough pace to string the field and leave ground for a late burst from off the pace.
scenarios.body: If the race is set up with enough pace to string the field and leave ground for a late burst from off the pace.

watchPoints.text: Watch for Zooter drifting toward an unexpected lead: with no natural front-runner declared and this horse's versatility over 10f on Good, Finley Marsh may push forward simply to avoid a traffic problem in a slow-run race.

Blue Jammin's win came exclusively on Soft ground — all four Good/Standard efforts have been blank, and if the Ffos Las surface rides on the faster end of Good tonight, its chance diminishes significantly.

Tales Old As Time returns after 237 days off for a lightly-resourced trainer; fitness on reappearance after such a lengthy break is a major unknown, particularly for a two-year-old stepping back into a competitive handicap.

With Liveinthelight, Rajwaah, Grand Pier, and Blue Jammin all naturally wanting to race from the rear, monitor the early canter to post — if any of these four are clearly on their toes or taken wide to get cover, it signals where Jamin, Wood, Vigors, or Dace intend to compromise on position.

Ffos Las's round, flat track and tight home turn tend to reward horses that travel well through the race rather than those making ground from a stand-still; any horse caught flat-footed in a crawl-then-sprint race shape is at a disadvantage, so watch the pace of the first half-mile.
